name: btree_balance_no_duplicates
targetProperty: For all B-tree balance operations, no cells are duplicated: each cell from the input pages appears exactly once in the output pages (injection from cell_array to output).

S0.label: S0
S0.content: No Duplicated Cells Property: During balance_non_root, each cell in cell_array.cell_payloads is written to exactly one position in exactly one output page. No cell appears twice in the output.

G1.label: G1
G1.content: Index Range Disjointness: Each page is assigned a disjoint range of cell indices from cell_array

G2.label: G2
G2.content: Single Write Per Cell: The edit_page function writes each cell exactly once to its assigned page
G2.formal: ∀ idx ∈ [start_new_cells, start_new_cells+number_new_cells): cell_array[idx] written exactly once

G3.label: G3
G3.content: No Aliasing: Cells in cell_array are distinct memory references (no pointer aliasing)

R1.label: R1

R2.label: R2
R2.content:
Single Write Per Cell is guaranteed by the edit_page and page_insert_array functions:

1. edit_page (line 6911) receives parameters:
   - start_new_cells: starting index in cell_array
   - number_new_cells: count of cells to write
   - These define the range [start_new_cells, start_new_cells + number_new_cells)

2. page_insert_array (lines 7239-7255) writes cells in a single loop:
   ```rust
   for i in 0..count {
       let payload = &cell_array.cell_payloads[first + i];
       // ... allocate space and copy
       buf[cell_content_area..cell_content_area + payload.len()].copy_from_slice(payload);
   }
   ```

3. Each cell at index (first + i) is written exactly once per page_insert_array call
4. The done[page_idx] flag (line 3804) ensures each page is processed exactly once
5. Since ranges are disjoint (G1), no cell index is passed to page_insert_array twice

The cell_content_area grows downward, ensuring each write occupies fresh memory.

R3.label: R3
R3.content:
No Aliasing: Cells in cell_array.cell_payloads point to distinct memory regions.

1. Cells from page content (lines 3058-3071):
   - Each cell is extracted via cell_get_raw_region which returns (cell_start, cell_len)
   - Cells within a page are stored at non-overlapping offsets (B-tree page format invariant)
   - Different pages have different memory buffers

2. Overflow cells (lines 3075-3080):
   - Each overflow cell has its own pinned payload buffer (Pin<Box<[u8]>>)
   - These are heap-allocated and distinct from page buffers

3. Divider cells from parent (lines 3092-3110):
   - Stored in reusable_divider_buffers[i] for each sibling
   - Each buffer is a separate Vec<u8> cleared and reused per sibling

4. The to_static_buf function (line 6907) simply transmutes the slice reference:
   ```rust
   fn to_static_buf(buf: &mut [u8]) -> &'static mut [u8] {
       unsafe { std::mem::transmute::<&mut [u8], &'static mut [u8]>(buf) }
   }
   ```
   This preserves the original memory location, so distinct source regions remain distinct.

5. Since cells come from disjoint sources (different pages or different regions within pages), cell_payloads entries cannot alias.
